Hi Devon — thanks for the clear brief. Below are three concise, actionable options we recommend for a 6-week pilot. Numbers below are pilot-only and do not lock long-term pricing:

1) Starter Pilot (lowest friction)
- Commitment: $6k flat fee for 6 weeks (covers up to 30M generated tokens)
- KV-cache incentive: one-time $1k token credit applied at activation (will offset early tokens for cold-starts)
- Quantization advisory: included (2 hours) + 4-hour optional deep-dive ($1,200)
- Technical support: Standard onboarding (2 sessions)

2) Performance Pilot (recommended if you expect measurable cost drop)
- Commitment: $14k for 6 weeks (covers up to 100M generated tokens)
- KV-cache incentive: 50% discounted rate on cached tokens during pilot window (applies to token billing only)
- Quantization advisory: included (6 hours) + optional model-specific eval credits (applies to your HubSpot record)
- SLA: soft SLOs for latency (best-effort), priority ops channel for pilot

3) Committed Trial (closest to production)
- Commitment: $28k (6 weeks) with optional rollover credits if you convert to Dedicated capacity within 90 days
- KV-cache incentive: 100% credit for first X cached requests (defined in term sheet) + 25% discount after credits
- Quantization advisory: included (10 hours) + two follow-up tuning sessions
- Extras: automatic fallback policy configuration and a short regression eval run

Notes on discounts and packaging:
- Discounts are pilot-only and modeled as token credits or temporary billing-rate adjustments (we avoid changing base MSRP for short pilots).
- If procurement prefers a PO-anchored credit (line item), we can provide an MSA addendum showing credit application rules.

I'll draft the worksheet to show per-token math and what a 25% and 50% reduction in token spend looks like under your expected throughput. Naomi — we'll attach the drafted spend table for Devon's procurement team.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Pilot ask — technical recommendations (quantization + cache)

Hi all — quick technical note to set expectations for the quantization and KV-cache parts of the proposal. This is meant to be short so procurement has the right context.

1) Quantization recommendations (BioBERT-ish, ~1k seq):
- Start with post-training static 8-bit quantization for embedding/dense layers to validate quality impact (lowest risk). Expect ~20–30% throughput improvement and modest cost reduction.
- If accuracy holds, we can move to mixed 4-bit kernels on attention-heavy layers (our hybrid 4/8 path). Typical wins there are another ~1.5–2x throughput for decode-heavy workloads; exact savings depend on tokenization patterns and sequence reuse.
- Key caveat: quantization can increase hallucination risk for some fine-tuned heads; we recommend a small eval set (~500 prompts) during week 1 of the pilot to track metric deltas.

2) KV-cache incentive mechanics:
- For your prefix-heavy workload, cached-token discount is the simplest to administer (we bill cached tokens at a reduced rate or apply a one-time cache token credit).
- If you want guaranteed cache hit behavior, we'll run a short warmup job (48–72h) to populate prefixes and measure effective cache hit rate before committing credits.

3) Ops notes:
- We can provide a lightweight eval harness and a shared results sheet. If you select Performance Pilot, we recommend enabling continuous prefix caching and the hybrid quantized runtime.

I'll be available for a 30-minute walkthrough if you want to go deeper into the quantization knobs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
